    {"name": "customer_urgency_signal", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Urgency signals plausibly affect prioritisation and resolution speed.     {"name": "workaround_available", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Presence of a workaround plausibly relates to resolution urgency/time.     {"name": "data_or_billing_sensitivity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Sensitivity flag is useful for identifying tickets needing careful handling. Dominated by not_present (200), reducing leverage somewhat, but values are well grounded (billing_discrepancy for the duplicate line item)."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.87,
  "source_groundedness": 0.84,
  "rationale": "The added columns provide multiple genuine, distinct axes (category, severity, scope, complexity, urgency, escalation, root cause) that let an analyst group and model resolution_minutes to answer how to reduce resolution time. There is mild redundancy between severity/scope and between category/root_cause, but each still contributes a separable dimension. Groundedness is generally strong: sampled values are sound readings of the source text, with silent rows correctly defaulting to not_present/no_urgency_stated. The softest spots are inferred numeric complexity and some confidently assigned escalation/root-cause labels, but no clear contradictions or invented facts were observed."
}
